title: Construct a DESeqDataSet from Pasilla counts and test treated versus untreated

sources.locator: Count matrix input, lines 411-496; About the pasilla dataset and Differential expression analysis, lines 642-696; model theory, lines 2430-2480

scientific_use: Build a gene-by-sample count object with aligned sample metadata, fit a negative-binomial GLM with design ~ condition, then return gene-level log2 fold changes and Wald-test p and adjusted p values for treated versus untreated Pasilla RNA-seq samples.
tool_role_basis: The vignette applies existing DESeq2 constructors, DESeq, and results to a supplied count matrix; it does not implement or change the statistical method.

inputs.meaning: Unnormalized integer gene counts, rows genes and columns seven Pasilla samples; the matrix columns must be aligned with metadata rows.
inputs.format: gzipped tab-separated matrix plus CSV sample annotations, imported as matrix/data.frame
inputs.stage: gene-level count matrix and sample metadata; upstream read alignment/count generation is outside this unit
inputs.source_example: The vignette loads package-copied extdata, strips 'fb' from metadata row names and reorders count columns to match; condition and sequencing type are factors.

outputs.meaning: Fitted DESeqDataSet with size factors, dispersion estimates and gene-wise GLM coefficients, then a DESeqResults table for log2(treated/untreated), Wald p values and adjusted p values.
outputs.stage: fitted model and extracted differential-expression result

dependencies: R and DESeq2 (package DESCRIPTION version 1.53.5 at pinned source)
SummarizedExperiment/Bioconductor classes and the package dependencies declared in DESCRIPTION
A valid design with replicated samples and correctly aligned count/metadata rows

evidence.claim: Inputs are raw/un-normalized integer counts, not library-size normalized values; the DESeqDataSet requires design metadata.
The exact two assets, factor columns, row-name normalization, and column reorder are shown.
The named Pasilla biological question is RNAi knock-down of the splicing factor pasilla in D. melanogaster cell cultures.

DESeq wraps size-factor estimation, dispersion estimation, and negative-binomial GLM fitting; results extracts LFC and Wald p/adjusted-p values and defaults to last design variable/level versus reference.

limitations: No model was executed in this inventory task; reported outputs are documented semantics, not observed results.
The compressed count matrix contents and row count were not downloaded or previewed. The seven samples and their metadata are source-reported by the annotation asset and Pasilla source vignette.
The vignette presents count generation as upstream and does not specify the exact production pipeline for the copied gene-level matrix in the inspected lines.
The default result contrast depends on factor reference/level ordering; task author must pin and grade the intended comparison explicitly.
Data reuse terms for the underlying study assets were not independently established; DESeq2 software licensing does not by itself establish data rights.

title: Adjust the Pasilla treatment analysis for sequencing type
scientific_use: Refit the Pasilla count data using ~ type + condition to account for single-read versus paired-end sequencing type while estimating the condition effect; optionally extract the sequencing-type contrast.
tool_role_basis: This composes existing DESeqDataSet mutation, DESeq, and results calls on an existing study dataset; no method implementation is changed.

inputs.meaning: The previously constructed/fitted Pasilla DESeqDataSet and sample variables condition and type.
inputs.stage: gene-level counts plus factor metadata; derived by the standard input workflow. The factor labels for type are simplified by removing the suffix beginning at hyphen.
inputs.source_example: A copy ddsMF <- dds is relabeled and refit; the treatment variable is placed last in the design. The source identifies type as sequencing protocol, not a biological condition.

outputs.meaning: Refitted model and extracted condition results adjusted for sequencing type; optional type single-versus-paired contrast.

dependencies: Upstream Pasilla matrix construction and factor alignment from deseq2-pasilla-standard-de
Full-rank design and sample metadata with both condition and type

evidence.claim: Pasilla includes a condition and sequencing type annotation; the latter reports sequencing protocol.
The vignette copies the fitted object, changes type labels, sets design ~ type + condition, reruns DESeq, and extracts condition or type contrasts.

limitations: The source describes a clearer treatment attribution as the motivation but provides no executed comparative estimates in the inspected block.
Sequencing-type adjustment does not establish causal separation if design is confounded or rank deficient; the author must inspect the actual design matrix and decide whether the example is suitable.
This is an alternative refit of the same study data, not independent replication or a new dataset.

title: Transform Pasilla counts for sample clustering and PCA quality assessment

sources.locator: Count data transformations and blind dispersion estimation, lines 1191-1289; sample clustering, distance heatmap and PCA, lines 1356-1440

scientific_use: Apply VST or rlog to normalized count data and assess sample similarity with distance clustering and PCA, visualizing condition and sequencing-type covariates for quality assessment and exploratory analysis.
tool_role_basis: The example applies existing DESeq2 transformations and plotting functions to the already constructed Pasilla object.

inputs.meaning: Pasilla DESeqDataSet with raw counts, design, condition and type annotations; prior DESeq dispersion fit is reused in the example.
inputs.stage: count matrix and fitted model; VST/rlog return normalized log-scale representation for downstream visualization, not differential testing
inputs.source_example: The vignette sets blind=FALSE after standard fitting and uses vst for distances/PCA; it also shows rlog and normalized-log transformation for comparisons.

outputs.meaning: Transformed gene-by-sample values; sample distance matrix/heatmap and PCA coordinates/plot with condition and type labels.
outputs.format: DESeqTransform, distance matrix, plots or returned PCA data.frame

dependencies: DESeq2; pheatmap for heatmaps; RColorBrewer for sample-distance heatmap; ggplot2 for customized PCA; optional vsn for mean-SD plot

evidence.claim: VST/rlog normalize for library size and aim to flatten experiment-wide mean-variance dependence; rlog can be slower for many samples.
Blind=TRUE re-estimates using intercept for unbiased sample comparison; blind=FALSE is advised for downstream transformation when many genes differ according to the design.
The example transforms fitted dds with blind=FALSE, computes sample distances and plots PCA against condition and type.

limitations: These transformations and PCA are for visualization/clustering, not replacements for raw counts in DESeq2 differential testing.
No plot or transformed matrix was generated during inspection.
The source says QC can precede or accompany differential expression; deciding sample exclusion requires external quality evidence and remains with the author.
rlog runtime discussion is source-reported for an example scale, not measured here.

title: Shrink Pasilla log2 fold changes for visualization and ranking

sources.locator: Log fold change shrinkage for visualization and ranking, lines 703-719
arguments and estimator descriptions, lines 26-58 and 99-110

scientific_use: Apply adaptive prior shrinkage to fitted treatment log2 fold changes to stabilize effect-size visualization and gene ranking, with apeglm shown in the vignette.
tool_role_basis: The vignette applies the existing lfcShrink API and an external estimator package; it does not implement the estimator.

inputs.meaning: A fitted Pasilla DESeqDataSet and named treatment coefficient condition_treated_vs_untreated.
inputs.source_example: The vignette inspects resultsNames(dds) and calls lfcShrink with type=apeglm.

outputs.meaning: DESeqResults containing shrunken log2 fold-change estimates for visualization/ranking.

dependencies: apeglm package for the demonstrated type

evidence.claim: The example's stated use is visualization and ranking and demonstrates apeglm using the named coefficient.
lfcShrink requires a fitted DESeqDataSet and supports apeglm, ashr and normal shrinkage types.

limitations: The apeglm package is suggested rather than imported by DESeq2; availability and version must be pinned for later execution.
No estimates were generated or compared in this inspection.

title: Import Salmon transcript quantifications into a gene-level DESeqDataSet

sources.locator: Transcript abundance files and tximport/tximeta, lines 256-359

sources.revision: package metadata says version 1.38.0, Bioconductor 3.22, commit 5c04cae dated 2025-10-29; retrieved 2026-09-30

scientific_use: Import Salmon transcript-level quantification files with transcript-to-gene mapping, then construct a DESeqDataSet using estimated gene counts and sample metadata for a later gene-level analysis.
tool_role_basis: This workflow composes tximport and DESeq2 constructors; it uses existing packages without implementing or changing the method.

inputs.meaning: Salmon quant.sf.gz files for six GEUVADIS RNA-seq samples in tximportData, a run/sample table and tx2gene mapping; demonstration creates condition labels A and B in code.
inputs.format: Compressed tabular Salmon quantifications, sample table and CSV transcript-to-gene map
inputs.stage: transcript abundance quantifier output; tximport summarizes to estimated gene counts and length-related information, not normalized counts
inputs.source_example: Paths are formed from sample run IDs; mapping file is named tx2gene.gencode.v27.csv. The vignette explicitly says the condition labels are artificial for demonstration.

outputs.meaning: tximport list of gene-level matrices and then ddsTxi with design ~ condition.
outputs.stage: imported gene-level estimated counts with sample metadata, before DESeq fitting

dependencies: R; tximport; tximportData demo package; readr; DESeq2
Quantifier output paths and matching transcript-to-gene map; later analysis requires valid design metadata

evidence.claim: Recommended import route uses transcript quantifier outputs, summarizes to gene-level estimated counts, and is not normalized-count input.
The example locates tximportData files, fabricates A/B condition labels, imports Salmon quant.sf.gz with a GENCODE v27 mapping and constructs design ~ condition.
tximportData package metadata identifies output from five named quantifiers on six GEUVADIS samples; this unit specifically uses the Salmon example.

limitations: The sample IDs, individual quantification files, mapping file rows, quantifier version and checksums were not inspected.
The A/B labels are code-created demonstration values and must not be treated as observed biological treatment groups.
No import or downstream model was run; package page metadata may differ from the version used by the mutable Bioconductor release source for the vignette.
tximportData license shown by the inspected package manual is GPL (>=2); permissions for the underlying GEUVADIS data and quantification assets were not separately determined.

title: Test a multi-term count-model contribution with a likelihood ratio test

sources.locator: Time-series experiments and Likelihood ratio test, lines 1624-1681
test, full and reduced arguments, lines 30-57

scientific_use: Compare a full negative-binomial GLM to a nested reduced model to test whether the omitted term set improves fit; useful for testing a multi-level factor or interaction terms jointly.
tool_role_basis: DESeq2 exposes test="LRT" and a reduced formula; the vignette documents application, not implementation of a new method.

inputs.meaning: A fitted-ready DESeqDataSet with a full design and a nested reduced design formula.
inputs.stage: raw-count dataset with sample design metadata
inputs.source_example: The simple ~condition versus ~1 and ~batch+condition versus ~batch examples are eval=FALSE; time-series designs are described conceptually with a link to an external RNA-seq workflow.

outputs.meaning: Gene-level LRT statistic and p value for all terms present in full but absent from reduced; results table's one LFC column is only one comparison and does not summarize all jointly tested effects.

dependencies: R; DESeq2; valid nested model formulas and count/design input

evidence.claim: The LRT compares full and reduced models and tests removed terms jointly; df is parameter-count difference.
The displayed calls specify test="LRT", reduced formula and results extraction, but are explicitly eval=FALSE.
LRT p values cover all removed variables/levels while the results table shows one LFC comparison.

limitations: This is a documented method with unevaluated generic examples, not evidence of a particular executed scientific analysis or dataset.
Task-specific design, contrasts, and biological meaning of the jointly tested term set remain for the author to define.
The external time-series workflow was not opened or inspected.
